root_cause.text: An off-by-one error in the validation of wire_order indices allowed a value equal to ARRAY_SIZE(config_pins) (i.e., 4), causing an out-of-bounds access when using that value as an index into the config_pins array, which has only 4 elements (indices 0–3).
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes the comparison from `>` to `>=` in `WARN_ON(wire_order[i] > ARRAY_SIZE(config_pins))`, and the commit message explicitly states that the original check allowed `wire_order[i]` to equal `ARRAY_SIZE(config_pins)`, leading to out-of-bounds access when used as an index in `config_pins[wire_order[i]]`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix off-by-one error in bounds check for config_pins array index.
intent_record.what: Changed the condition in WARN_ON from 'wire_order[i] > ARRAY_SIZE(config_pins)' to 'wire_order[i] >= ARRAY_SIZE(config_pins)'.
intent_record.how: This corrects the boundary check: the new condition triggers a warning and returns -EINVAL when wire_order[i] is greater than or equal to the array size, preventing out-of-bounds access. Previously, the check allowed the index equal to the array size, which is invalid.
